review.evidencePolicy: Retained decisions and public encounter state only; no secret check outcomes were used for tactical scoring.

findings: Short-range Dominate caused melee-capable vampires to inherit an overly defensive caster posture.
Wall of Ice used a fixed virtual-damage value and had no allied-wall saturation term.
See the Unseen treated every Hidden or Undetected opponent as a qualifying target.
Pit jump planning did not test run-up and jump segments against managed ice-wall geometry.
changes: Classify melee actors with no hostile spell beyond 30 feet as short-range hybrids.
Reward route progress only when the caster has no useful current action and at least two actions remain.
Score Wall of Ice by proximity, apparent combat role, caster injury and intact allied-wall saturation.
Require observer-known Invisibility before valuing See the Unseen; ordinary Hidden remains private observer state.
Reject Leap and Long Jump routes whose run-up or airborne segment crosses an intact managed Wall of Ice.
limits: Wall of Ice placement remains straight horizontal or vertical supported geometry.
The planner does not predict future wall destruction or arbitrary multi-turn ally routes.
Incorporeal creatures inside objects and suspected illusions need explicit observer knowledge before See the Unseen can be scored.
A fresh live fight is required to compare emergent initiative, dice and player choices.
